partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. Recorded English and national or official-language queries and retrieved primary governance evidence support medium confidence. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

News search from 17 October 2026 in English and Estonian, with the justice and digital affairs ministry's website (news titles readable but undated) and its search page (newest 14 October, before the window). Left for review: Estonia's place on the endorsement list of the French presidency's Paris Call for AI Safety and Security, published on 9 November and since updated. The consumer protection and technical regulatory authority's AI page, last updated 10 September, repeats a supervisory role already in the record, and no Estonian announcement of the endorsement was found. No new national evaluator or final designation act was found. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

Owner-requested check of 23 November 2026 of a reader's lead on an Estonian AI safety body: the government's, interior ministry's, information system authority's, consumer protection authority's and economy ministry's news for 2024 to 2026, the justice and digital ministry's AI items, the Estonian Academy of Security Sciences' pages and news, the adopted Digital Society Development Plan 2035 and the 2027-2030 digital programme. Added as closest body the academy's Secure AI Knowledge Centre initiative (T3), which by the academy's own account is to become a knowledge centre once funding and partners are found; no government act concerning it and no testing work were found. The Estonia-Finland joint letter of 11 November 2026 and the Prime Minister's statement of 14 November 2026 call for independent EU-level evaluation of the most advanced models and name no national body. Status unchanged. Partial check, not a full record re-check.

check.language_note: The recorded et query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. Preserved result batches, using 1-based positions in check.searches: EE-search = searches 1, 2 (en, et). Each multi-query batch has only a combined returned result set; its source_ids cannot be attributed to individual queries. Historical query dates are recorded as 17 October 2026 in the phase6 search-boundary ledger.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.

excerpts.text: Sisekaitseakadeemia sellest aastast alustanud turvalise tehisaru teadmuskeskuse (T3) initsiatiiviga
excerpts.gloss: the Academy of Security Sciences has this year started the safe-AI knowledge centre (T3) initiative

excerpts.text: Selliseid organisatsioone on üle maailma veel – Suurbritanniast ja Singapurist kuni Kanada ja Koreani. Nende ühine nimetaja on tehisaru turvalisus ja/või julgeolek (AI Safety/Security).
excerpts.gloss: There are other such organisations in the world, from the UK and Singapore to Canada and Korea. Their common denominator is AI safety and/or security.

excerpts.text: the Estonian Academy of Security Sciences, as a development partner in smart security, has this year launched the Secure AI Knowledge Centre initiative, known as T3.

Once funding and cooperation partners have been secured, this initiative will develop into the T3 Knowledge Centre, focusing on the security dimension of artificial intelligence – security risks and their mitigation.
Similar organisations already exist around the world, from the United Kingdom and Singapore to Canada and Korea. Their common denominator is AI safety and/or security.
